version: "0.1"
title: Priority Job Scheduler CLI
objective: A single-file, stdlib-only Python CLI (scheduler.py) that manages jobs with priorities and dependencies, persists them in scheduler.json and executes them in dependency order with priority tiebreak.
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: Empty Python project; deliverable is scheduler.py at the repository root with unittest tests in tests/.
  assumptions:
    - "Job ids match ^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32}$ and are case-sensitive."
    - "Priority is an integer 1-10 (bool and non-integers rejected)."
    - "scheduler.json lives in the current working directory, overridable by a --file option."
    - "Invalid input exits with code 1 and a message on stderr; success exits 0."
    - "run-next simulates execution: it marks the job running, persists nothing intermediate that matters, then marks it done."
    - "fail <id> applies to a pending, ready or running job; an unknown id or a job already done, failed or cancelled is an error."
    - "A job whose dependency is failed or cancelled is cancelled; cancelled jobs never become ready."
    - "Adding a job that depends on a failed or cancelled job is allowed and the new job is created cancelled."
    - "report prints per-status counts and the execution order of non-terminal jobs."
constraints:
  - Single file scheduler.py using only the Python standard library.
  - The status ready is never written to scheduler.json.
  - No real job execution, no concurrency, no network, no removal or editing of jobs.
success_criteria:
  - All boundary tests pass.
  - Every rule of the request is covered by an obligation.
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "Adding a job validates id format, priority range, duplicate id, self-dependency and unknown dependencies, and rejects invalid jobs without changing the stored state.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h2, description: "Adding a job that would create a dependency cycle is rejected and the stored state is unchanged.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h3, description: "The execution order is a topological order where, among available jobs, higher priority comes first.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h4, description: "On load, every pending job whose depends_on are all done becomes ready, and ready is never written to scheduler.json.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h5, description: "When a job fails, all of its transitive dependents become cancelled.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h6, description: "run-next picks the highest-priority ready job, marks it running, then done.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h7, description: "The CLI provides add, run-next, fail, status and report commands over scheduler.json.", confidence: 0.85}
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Implement scheduler.py", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Write unittest boundary tests in tests/test_scheduler.py", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Run the gate", type: validate, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]}
required_evidence:
  - "Output of python3 -m unittest discover -s tests with all tests passing"
  - "Gate report ending in RESULT: PASS"
decision_rules:
  - "If a requirement is ambiguous, stop and ask the user."
  - "Anything outside the obligations is a spec amendment."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a Priority Job Scheduler CLI in Python (single file scheduler.py, stdlib only). Jobs: id (alphanumeric and underscore, 1-32 chars, unique), name, priority (1-10), depends_on (list of ids). Validation on add: reject duplicate id, self-dependency, unknown dependency. Cycle detection: reject any add that would create a cycle. Execution order: topological order with priority as tiebreak (higher first). A job is ready when it is pending and all of its depends_on are done; recompute on load. Failure propagation: when a job fails, all transitive dependents become cancelled. Status values: pending, ready, running, done, failed, cancelled. run-next: takes the highest-priority ready job, marks it running, then done (simulated). Persistence in scheduler.json; ready is never persisted, it is recomputed on load. Commands: add, run-next, fail <id>, status, report."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "id alphanumeric and underscore 1-32 chars"
      - "priority 1-10"
      - "reject duplicate id"
      - "reject self-dependency"
      - "reject unknown dependency"
      - "reject cycle"
      - "topological order with priority tiebreak"
      - "ready recomputed on load"
      - "ready never persisted"
      - "failure cancels transitive dependents"
      - "run-next highest-priority ready job"
      - "commands add run-next fail status report"
formal:
  module: JobScheduler
  obligations:
    - id: id_and_priority_format
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Ids not matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32} and priorities outside integers 1-10 are rejected on add with exit 1."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["id alphanumeric and underscore 1-32 chars", "priority 1-10"]
      test: "test_scheduler.ValidationTests.test_id_and_priority_format"
    - id: duplicate_rejected
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Adding an existing id is rejected and scheduler.json is unchanged."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["reject duplicate id"]
      test: "test_scheduler.ValidationTests.test_duplicate_id_rejected"
    - id: self_dependency_rejected
      kind: boundary
      statement: "A job listing its own id in depends_on is rejected."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["reject self-dependency"]
      test: "test_scheduler.ValidationTests.test_self_dependency_rejected"
    - id: unknown_dependency_rejected
      kind: boundary
      statement: "A depends_on id that is not an existing job is rejected."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["reject unknown dependency"]
      test: "test_scheduler.ValidationTests.test_unknown_dependency_rejected"
    - id: cycle_rejected
      kind: boundary
      statement: "An add that would create a dependency cycle is rejected and state is unchanged."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["reject cycle"]
      test: "test_scheduler.CycleTests.test_cycle_rejected"
    - id: order_topological_priority
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The execution order lists every dependency before its dependents and, among available jobs, higher priority first."
      hypotheses: [h3]
      must_include: ["topological order with priority tiebreak"]
      test: "test_scheduler.OrderTests.test_topological_with_priority_tiebreak"
    - id: ready_recomputed_on_load
      kind: boundary
      statement: "A pending job whose depends_on are all done is ready after load, even if the file says pending."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["ready recomputed on load"]
      test: "test_scheduler.ReadyTests.test_ready_recomputed_on_load"
    - id: ready_not_persisted
      kind: boundary
      statement: "scheduler.json never contains the status ready."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["ready never persisted"]
      test: "test_scheduler.ReadyTests.test_ready_never_persisted"
    - id: failure_cancels_dependents
      kind: boundary
      statement: "fail marks the job failed and every transitive dependent cancelled; unrelated jobs are untouched."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["failure cancels transitive dependents"]
      test: "test_scheduler.FailureTests.test_failure_cancels_transitive_dependents"
    - id: run_next_picks_highest
      kind: boundary
      statement: "run-next runs the highest-priority ready job, ending it done; with no ready job it reports so."
      hypotheses: [h6]
      must_include: ["run-next highest-priority ready job"]
      test: "test_scheduler.RunNextTests.test_run_next_highest_priority"
    - id: commands_available
      kind: boundary
      statement: "add, run-next, fail, status and report all run through the CLI and persist in scheduler.json."
      hypotheses: [h7]
      must_include: ["commands add run-next fail status report"]
      test: "test_scheduler.CliTests.test_all_commands"
scope:
  paths: ["scheduler.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
EOF
export PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness
python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/job-scheduler/spec.yaml --formal && python3 -m forgemyspec package forgemyspec-bundle/job-scheduler/spec.yaml && python3 -m forgemyspec board start R1; python3 -m forgemyspec board

The spec is written and passes lint at 100/100 with no warnings. It is a spec-only bundle: every rule is a Python boundary test, with no Dafny proof. The bundle is in `forgemyspec-bundle/job-scheduler/`.

I haven't written any code yet. I also couldn't create `forgemyspec-board.yaml`: the guard blocks it until a spec covers it, so there is no board to show yet.

**Obligations** (all `boundary` kind, each tied to one test in `tests/test_scheduler.py`):

| id | Statement |
|---|---|
| `id_and_priority_format` | An id outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32}`, or a priority outside integers 1-10, is rejected on add with exit 1. |
| `duplicate_rejected` | Adding an existing id is rejected and `scheduler.json` is unchanged. |
| `self_dependency_rejected` | A job listing its own id in `depends_on` is rejected. |
| `unknown_dependency_rejected` | A `depends_on` id that isn't an existing job is rejected. |
| `cycle_rejected` | An add that would create a cycle is rejected and the state is unchanged. |
| `order_topological_priority` | Dependencies come before their dependents; among available jobs, higher priority comes first. |
| `ready_recomputed_on_load` | A pending job whose dependencies are all done is ready after load. |
| `ready_not_persisted` | `scheduler.json` never contains the status `ready`. |
| `failure_cancels_dependents` | `fail` marks the job failed and every transitive dependent cancelled; unrelated jobs are untouched. |
| `run_next_picks_highest` | `run-next` runs the highest-priority ready job, ending it done; with no ready job it reports so. |
| `commands_available` | `add`, `run-next`, `fail`, `status` and `report` all work through the CLI and persist. |

**Assumptions I made.** Say so if any is wrong:
- **Ids:** they are case-sensitive.
- **Priority:** it must be an integer, so booleans and other types are rejected.
- **File location:** the file is `scheduler.json` in the current directory, with a `--file` option to change it.
- **Errors:** bad input exits 1 with a message on stderr.
- **`run-next`:** it marks the job running and then done within the same call.
- **`fail <id>`:** it works on a pending, ready or running job. An unknown id, or a job already done, failed or cancelled, is an error.
- **Cancelled jobs:** they never become ready. A job added with a dependency that is already failed or cancelled is created as cancelled.
- **`report`:** it prints counts per status and the execution order of the jobs not yet finished.
